name: payabl.
description: payabl. provides payment acceptance and business account services for merchants. Its products cover online checkout, card acquiring, local payment methods, in-store acceptance and recurring payments. The payabl.one platform brings payment, settlement and account information into a shared workspace. This scenario focuses on UK and European merchant procurement.
criteria: Supported merchant countries and payment methods

claims: The UK site presents online payments, in-store acceptance, business accounts and a shared management platform.
The group lists offices in London, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Limassol and Vilnius.
The company identifies separate UK and Cyprus regulated entities; product availability should be checked for the contracting entity.
The gateway product combines card acquiring with local payment methods and several checkout integration options.
The UK in-store product supports payment terminals, contactless acceptance and reporting connected to payabl.one.
payabl.one presents payment, settlement, account and dispute information in a single workspace.
The published payment method directory includes cards, digital wallets and local bank payment options.
The recurring payments offering addresses scheduled collections and subscription merchant use cases.
The fraud product describes Sift integration, merchant rules, authentication and dispute monitoring.
In its September 2024 product announcement, payabl. reported serving more than 500 businesses in Europe and Latin America. This is historical scale evidence, not a current merchant count.
The December 2025 review reported an approximately 30-person London team and a new Vilnius entity, supporting a specialist European B2B scale assumption.
The Paypers interviewed payabl.'s CEO about its acquiring business and merchant payment requirements in February 2022.

targetAudience: Merchant finance, payments and risk teams

dos: Use verified product pages and dated company announcements.
Distinguish merchant eligibility, supported markets and contracting entities.
Discuss payment operations and procurement in practical terms.
donts: Promise merchant approval, authorisation rates, guaranteed settlement or fraud elimination.
Invent processing prices, customer testimonials or regulatory permissions.
Present scenario traffic or future measurements as actual results.

unknowns: GB selects the UK merchant market for this scenario; the group also operates through other European entities.
The published 500-plus business figure is dated September 2024 and is not a current merchant count.
Traffic scale and 8% monthly growth are illustrative scenario assumptions, not measured payabl. analytics or forecasts.
Product eligibility, pricing, reserve terms and settlement conditions depend on the merchant and contract.

copy.introduction: For UK and European merchants, compare payment providers by supported markets, payment methods, integration requirements, commercial terms and operating controls. Confirm the relevant contracting entity and merchant eligibility during procurement.
copy.positiveCompany: offers payment services that merchants can assess against their sales channels, integration needs, supported markets and risk controls.
copy.neutralCompany: is another payment provider to compare against the merchant's operating requirements and proposed commercial terms.
copy.fallback: Build a payment provider shortlist around merchant eligibility, integration requirements, supported payment methods, reporting, settlement terms and support. Confirm product scope directly with each provider.
